findings.summary: The projected 1,807,231 data rows exceed Excel's 1,048,576-row worksheet limit (and a header would reduce usable data capacity further), yet the export passes every row to a single worksheet without enforcing EXCEL_MAX_ROWS. The default annual export therefore cannot satisfy the single-sheet capacity requirement and may fail, truncate data, or produce an unusable workbook.

Nested flatMap/map operations materialize the entire projected 1.8-million-object dataset in browser memory before workbook generation, with no streaming, batching, or size rejection. This leaves the required default download vulnerable to browser memory exhaustion or unresponsiveness.

unverified: No implementation of writeSingleBrowserWorksheet is supplied, so its failure behavior, row-limit handling, download behavior, and any silent truncation cannot be verified.
No tests are supplied demonstrating that the default annual export remains downloadable, preserves/reconciles all source records, or handles worksheet and browser capacity boundaries.

findings.summary: displayedClosing subtracts only expense and fx_eur consumptions, omitting the supported fx_other category. With the observed fx_other total of 1494440 TRY, the displayed closing balance is overstated by exactly 1494440 TRY and cannot reconcile for all supported consumption types.
The change only computes and returns a closing value; it does not display or return the required exact opening, inflow, outflow, conversion, and closing turnover for every pool consumer category.

unverified: No tests are shown, so exact reconciliation behavior for expense and fx_eur, numeric precision/stability for TRY amounts, and handling of malformed or unknown consumption types cannot be verified.

findings.summary: Each detail amount is rounded independently, with no residual-cent reconciliation against the rounded source total. Consequently the returned amounts can sum above or below the source amount (for example, allocating 0.01 with shares [0.5, 0.5] returns 0.02), violating exact-to-cent preservation and matching the reported aggregate-drift failure mode.

unverified: No tests are shown for exact reconciliation across representative row counts, fractional shares, negative amounts, or zero/empty shares.
The required behavior when shares do not sum to 1, contain negative/non-finite values, or when source is non-finite cannot be verified from the supplied material.
JavaScript number arithmetic may be unsuitable for all supported currency magnitudes and decimal inputs; supported numeric bounds and overflow/precision behavior are unspecified.

findings.summary: The verify script removes `prisma generate`, so generated clients are not refreshed before typecheck after schema changes, directly violating the release-gate requirement.
`tsc --noEmit || echo existing Prisma mismatch` converts every TypeScript failure into a successful script exit, allowing genuine typecheck failures to pass the release gate.
Temporary reviewer-only probe is included in the release tree, directly violating the requirement to ship only product and durable public methodology artifacts.
Private root-cause scratch notes are included in the release tree, directly violating the frozen acceptance criteria.
